patches.summary: Hoist the __requestid generation above the retry loop in client.go so all retries for the same logical request share the same idempotency token.
patches.reason: Greptile P1 on PR #471: __requestid was generated inline inside the retry loop, so each retry attempt got a different epoch_ms+random token. The server treats __requestid as the idempotency key, so distinct values across retries make the second + third attempts look like fresh requests instead of replays — exactly what idempotency is meant to prevent. Generating the id once before `for attempt := 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++` and reusing it on every retry restores the intended semantics. GET requests still skip the header (requestID stays empty for GETs).
patches.validated_outcome: Build / vet / 92 tests / verify-skill all clean after the change.

patches.summary: Added Chrome cookie import, local order history, cart planning, checkout, analytics, config defaults, and agent-context enrichment.
patches.reason: The generated OrderToGo CLI needed the requested agent-safe ordering workflow without re-running the Printing Press generator.
patches.validated_outcome: Build, vet, required command smoke checks, verify fixture, config dry-run, and validate-narrative passed with a workspace-local GOCACHE.

patches.summary: Three fixes for a fully-broken published CLI: implement real Chrome cookie decryption on macOS, spoof browser-like UA + Origin + Referer on every API call, and rewrite orders place to use the real POST /m/api/postmicmeshorder endpoint with Stripe saved-card auth.
patches.reason: As-published the CLI failed at three layers. (1) third_party/kooky/browser/chrome/chrome.go read encrypted_value as raw bytes and never decrypted them, so auth login --chrome silently imported zero cookies on macOS. (2) Even with valid cookies, ordertogo.com returned 403 Access denied for every /m/api/* call because the server gates on browser-like User-Agent + Origin + Referer headers and the CLI sent ordertogo-pp-cli/0.1.0 with no Origin. (3) The generated orders place command drove a headless-Chrome Braintree DropIn flow that the live site does not use; the real checkout endpoint is /m/api/postmicmeshorder and the payment processor is Stripe with a saved customer + card key.
patches.validated_outcome: Build and vet pass. auth login --chrome now imports 8 cookies on macOS (verified end-to-end against a live ordertogo.com session). Live /m/api/* requests return real responses (menu fetch, restaurant detail) instead of 403. PRINTING_PRESS_VERIFY=1 dry-run of orders place produces a request body byte-for-byte identical to the postmicmeshorder body captured from a real successful $2.99 checkout in the browser.

patches.summary: Switch orders list from /m/api/getmicmeshorders (web SHOW path) to /api/getUserOrderHistoryByUserid (real LIST endpoint). Inject Authorization (from _fbtoken cookie) and __requestid headers globally. Resolve and cache meshuser id via /api/getRestmeshUser.
patches.reason: As shipped, `orders list` posted to /m/api/getmicmeshorders with empty body and got 400 'Server communication config missing'. That endpoint is the per-orderid SHOW path; the actual LIST endpoint /api/getUserOrderHistoryByUserid was missed during sniff. All /api/* calls also require Authorization=<_fbtoken JWT> (the web client lifts the cookie value into the header in fbbase.post) plus an __requestid idempotency header on POSTs. Without those headers every call returns the same 'Server communication config missing'. Fix: client.go injects both headers automatically; orders_list.go and sync.go's orders branch do a two-call flow (getRestmeshUser to obtain meshuser.id, then getUserOrderHistoryByUserid) and cache the id on Config.MeshUserID after the first lookup.
patches.validated_outcome: ordertogo-pp-cli orders list returns 58 real orders (Sep 2025 through May 2026). sync --orders ingests 58 rows. Verified against the same user account whose live /history page renders the same 58 entries from /api/getUserOrderHistoryByUserid.

patches.summary: orders place now populates postOrderResult.TrackURL from order.orderToken, and verifyMode redacts CustomerName plus paymentCard firstname/lastname alongside the other PII fields.
patches.reason: Greptile P2 #1: TrackURL was declared on postOrderResult but never assigned, so agent callers could not deep-link to the tracking page after a successful order. The web client builds /trackorder/<restname>/<orderid> by splitting order.orderToken (mesh.order.js micmeshCheckout success); mirror that. Greptile P2 #2: verifyMode redacted StripeCustomer, DefaultCardMap, PaymentCard.PhoneNum, and CustomerPhone but left CustomerName plus paymentCard firstname/lastname in plaintext, so PRINTING_PRESS_VERIFY=1 dumps leaked the account holder's full name.
patches.validated_outcome: Build, vet pass. PRINTING_PRESS_VERIFY=1 dry-run now redacts all six PII fields (customername, customerphone, paymentCard.firstname/lastname/phonenum, st_cus_id) and DefaultCardMap. Response parser captures order.orderToken so postOrderResult.TrackURL is populated for downstream tooling.

patches.summary: Drop the dead `item_id` string field from the localStorageCart shape and document why the int `id` is the menu-item id the postmicmeshorder body wants.
patches.reason: Greptile P1 (PR #471): localStorageCart.Items[] had both `id int` and `item_id string`, but only `id` was mapped into cartItem.ItemID, leaving the string field as a silent dead member. Greptile correctly flagged the ambiguity. The byte-for-byte validation against a captured real $2.99 checkout confirmed `id` is what the API wants; removing the string field eliminates the ambiguity for future readers.
patches.validated_outcome: Build, vet pass. Request body remains byte-for-byte identical to the captured real checkout body. PRINTING_PRESS_VERIFY=1 dry-run unchanged.

patches.summary: Reject the `v11` Chrome cookie prefix on macOS/Linux instead of decrypting it as AES-128-CBC and emitting garbage.
patches.reason: Greptile P2 (PR #471): `v11` is the Windows App-Bound Encryption marker (AES-256-GCM with per-cookie nonce + tag), not a macOS/Linux variant of AES-128-CBC. The previous check accepted both `v10` and `v11` and ran AES-128-CBC on the v11 ciphertext, which would silently fail PKCS#7 validation or produce garbled output if Chrome ever started emitting v11 cookies on macOS/Linux.
patches.validated_outcome: Build, vet pass. The kooky chrome decrypter now returns a specific 'App-Bound Encryption is Windows-only' error if it ever sees `v11` on macOS/Linux, with the runtime.GOOS in the message.
